skill.name: harness-model-protocol
skill.description: Analyze how agent frameworks translate messages, tools, streaming events, and system prompts between harness code and LLM provider APIs.
skill.summary: Map the protocol layer between agent harnesses and LLM provider APIs.
skill.author: Dowwie

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline protocol examples, and report-template prompts. I found no executable shell commands, no real network calls, no prompt injection attempt, and no intent to extract hidden system instructions.

remediation.issue: Static analysis flags many Markdown backticks as Ruby or shell execution.
remediation.suggestion: Keep code examples inside clearly labeled documentation blocks and avoid ambiguous snippets that resemble executable shell instructions.

remediation.issue: System prompt examples can be mistaken for prompt extraction attempts.
remediation.suggestion: State that prompt assembly examples refer to application code under review, not the current assistant system prompt.

content.value_statement: Agent framework audits often miss the translation layer between internal state and provider APIs. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through message formats, tool calls, streaming events, and provider abstractions.
actual_capabilities: Compares OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and custom message wire formats.
Maps how tool schemas are sent to LLM APIs and parsed from responses.
Examines streaming event handling, including partial tool call accumulation.
Catalogs agentic primitives such as system prompts, scratchpads, interrupts, and confirmations.
Produces a structured markdown analysis with code references and architecture implications.
Identifies provider abstraction patterns such as thin adapters, unified clients, and gateways.
limitations: Requires access to the target framework source code to produce useful references.
Does not execute or benchmark LLM provider calls.
Does not replace a full security review of tool execution or credential handling.
May need a separate codebase mapping step for large or unfamiliar repositories.

use_cases.title: Review an agent framework protocol layer
use_cases.description: Map how a framework converts internal messages and tool calls into provider-specific API requests.

use_cases.title: Compare provider adapter designs
use_cases.description: Evaluate whether OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and local model adapters use a thin or unified abstraction.

use_cases.title: Document streaming and tool-call behavior
use_cases.description: Create a clear report on streaming events, partial JSON handling, tool result attribution, and human approval points.

prompt_templates.title: Basic protocol overview
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with a quick map of the harness to model boundary.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use harness-model-protocol to summarize how this framework sends messages to its LLM provider and receives responses.

prompt_templates.title: Tool call encoding review
prompt_templates.scenario: Focus on tool schemas and response parsing.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use harness-model-protocol to trace how tool definitions are encoded for the model and how tool calls are parsed back into framework actions.

prompt_templates.title: Streaming behavior analysis
prompt_templates.scenario: Audit streaming and partial tool call handling.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use harness-model-protocol to analyze streaming event types, partial argument accumulation, and final tool call reconstruction in this codebase.

prompt_templates.title: Multi-provider architecture comparison
prompt_templates.scenario: Produce a deeper architecture report across providers.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use harness-model-protocol to compare provider adapters, message translation, tool choice support, graceful degradation, and implications for a new framework design.

output_examples.input: Analyze a framework that supports OpenAI and Anthropic tool calling.
output_examples.output: A markdown report identifying the wire format family, adapter locations, tool schema transmission method, response parsing strategy, and key tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: Review streaming support in an agent runtime.
output: Explains how partial tool arguments are accumulated.
Notes whether tool calls are safely finalized before execution.

output_examples.input: Compare provider abstraction strategies for a new agent framework.
output_examples.output: A concise comparison of thin adapters, unified clients, and gateway translation, with recommendations based on observed code patterns.

best_practices: Run codebase mapping first when provider adapter files are not obvious.
Ask for file and line references for each protocol claim in the final report.
Review tool execution security separately from wire-format translation.
anti_patterns: Do not assume OpenAI-compatible APIs behave the same across all providers.
Do not treat streaming text deltas and tool argument deltas as the same event type.
Do not document prompt assembly without checking how dynamic context is inserted.

faq.question: What does this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It analyzes the protocol boundary between an agent harness and LLM provider APIs, including messages, tools, streaming, and prompts.

faq.question: Does it call external LLM APIs?
faq.answer: No. The skill is written as an analysis guide and does not perform network requests by itself.

faq.question: Which providers does it help compare?
faq.answer: It includes patterns for OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and local or custom providers.

faq.question: Can it find tool-call parsing bugs?
faq.answer: It can guide a review of parsing logic and partial streaming behavior, but it does not run tests automatically.

faq.question: Is this a security skill?
faq.answer: It can support security reviews of protocol handling, but its main category is code and architecture analysis.

faq.question: What output should I expect?
faq.answer: Expect a structured markdown document with protocol findings, provider comparisons, code references, and design implications.
